question: In 1700, the fortified settlement of Calcutta was named Fort William. Who was appointed as its first President and Governor of the Council?
explanation: In 1700, Bengal was made a separate Presidency independent of Madras. The fortified factory was named Fort William (after King William III), and Sir Charles Eyre was appointed as its first President.

question: Which rebellion in Bengal in 1696 provided the English East India Company with the excuse to fortify their factory at Sutanuti, which later grew into Fort William?
explanation: The rebellion of Sobha Singh (a zamindar of Burdwan) in 1696 against the Mughal authority in Bengal gave the English and Dutch the excuse to seek permission from Governor Ibrahim Khan to fortify their respective factories at Sutanuti (Calcutta) and Chinsurah.
